problems.memo_sentence: The authors state that their algorithm for option pricing provides a quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo, with AE achieving O(1/M) convergence and, under a first-order small-c approximation, still attaining O(M^(-2/3))—faster than Monte Carlo—with higher-order arithmetic restoring the full O(1/M) rate.
problems.source_evidence:
With this first order approximation the convergence rate of AE is
O(M −2/3) when c is properly chosen which is already
faster than classical Monte Carlo methods [17]. We
can recover the O(M −1) convergence rate of AE by
using higher orders implemented with quantum arith-
metic. The resulting circuits, however, have more
gates. This trade-oﬀ, discussed in Ref. [17], also gives
a formula that speciﬁes which value of c to use to
minimize the estimation error made when using AE.
problems.explanation: The paper is careful to tie the O(M^-2/3) scaling and the higher-order trade-off to prior work [17]; the memo presents these details as if they were fully established properties of this paper’s algorithm without noting that the trade-off and analysis come from previous work.

problems.memo_sentence: Classical Monte Carlo is explicitly taken as the main baseline, noted for its flexibility and O(M^(-1/2)) convergence, against which the AE-based quantum algorithm is contrasted as offering quadratic convergence-rate improvement.
